record.original_question: Let L be the closure on UC_b(R, R) of the differential operator (Lf)(x) = a(x)f''(x) + b(x)f'(x) + c(x)f(x), where a, b, c are bounded uniformly continuous real-valued functions and a(x) >= a_0 > 0 for all x. Find an explicitly given Chernoff function S(t) for L such that S is Chernoff-equivalent to the semigroup (e^{tL}), there exist a dense subspace D and constants M > 0, q > 1, n_0 > 0 with ||e^{tL}f - S(t/n)^n f|| <= M / q^n for all n >= n_0 and all f in D, and the formula for S(t) depends explicitly on a, b, c, f, and x without hiding the unknown semigroup inside the definition.

evidence.quote: Problem 30 (Super-fast converging Chernoff approximations example). Provide a meaningful example of Chernoff approximations that converge to a C0 -semigroup at least exponentially or prove that it is not possible in a meaningful setting.

The problem is to find a family (S(t))t≥0 of everywhere defined linear bounded operators in UCb (R, R) which has the following three properties: S and L satisfy the conditions of at least one version of the Chernoff theorem on approximation of operator semigroups; there exists a dense linear subspace D in UCb (R, R) and constants M > 0, q > 1, n0 > 0 such that ketL f − S(t/n)n f k ≤ M/q n for all n ≥ n0 and all f ∈ D; and S is defined by an explicitly given formula ... free from circulus vitiosus of any kind.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ denote the Banach space of bounded uniformly continuous real-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the supremum norm $\|\cdot\|$. Let $a, b, c \in UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ with $a(x) \geq a_0 > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Consider the differential operator defined on $C_b^2(\mathbb{R}) \cap UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ by
$$(L_0 f)(x) = a(x) f''(x) + b(x) f'(x) + c(x) f(x),$$
and let $L$ be its closure in $UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$. Assume that $L$ generates a strongly continuous semigroup $(e^{tL})_{t \geq 0}$ on $UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$.

Recall that a family $(S(t))_{t \geq 0}$ of bounded linear operators on $UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ is called Chernoff-equivalent to $(e^{tL})_{t \geq 0}$ if $S(0) = I$, $t \mapsto S(t)f$ is strongly continuous, $\|S(t)\| \leq e^{\omega t}$ for some $\omega \in \mathbb{R}$, and $\lim_{n	o\infty}\|(S(t/n))^n f - e^{tL} f\| = 0$ for every $f$ in a suitable core, uniformly on compact $t$-intervals.

Construct an explicit family $(S(t))_{t \geq 0}$ such that:
(i) $(S(t))_{t \geq 0}$ is Chernoff-equivalent to $(e^{tL})_{t \geq 0}$;
(ii) there exist a dense linear subspace $D \subset UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ and constants $M > 0$, $q > 1$, $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$$\|e^{tL} f - S(t/n)^n f\| \leq M q^{-n} \qquad 	ext{for all } n \geq n_0 	ext{ and all } f \in D;$$
(iii) the formula defining $(S(t)f)(x)$ is given explicitly in terms of $a$, $b$, $c$, $f$, $x$, and $t$, without referring to the semigroup $(e^{tL})$ itself or to any other implicitly defined object.

Alternatively, prove that no such family $(S(t))_{t \geq 0}$ exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent collection of open problems on Chernoff approximations of operator semigroups. No published resolution providing such an explicit super-fast (exponentially convergent) Chernoff approximation for general second-order elliptic operators with bounded uniformly continuous coefficients on $UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ was located.
